prompted_by: an independent reviewer's argument, relayed verbatim; checked against the code, not accepted on authority

items.quote: The mutex leak this diff fixes also stranded a second waiter class beyond the one the pull request names, since `balancer_child.go`'s init-timer callback takes the same lock.
items.asserted_defect: The pre-fix mutex leak in run() could also permanently block the balancer_child.go init-timer AfterFunc's cb.parent.mu.Lock() call, not just UpdateClientConnState, making the pre-existing bug's scope broader than the PR describes.
items.asserted_consequence: A second class of goroutine (the per-child init-timer callback, already dispatched and blocked on the mutex) can be left permanently blocked whenever the pre-fix leak occurs and it loses the race for the freed mutex to the leaking run() goroutine, beyond the UpdateClientConnState caller the PR names.
items.priority_note: Filed as a plain, unlabeled, non-blocking observation, which is the correct level for a true-but-sub-threshold, already-fixed pre-existing scope expansion.
items.action_note: Not used to justify any blocking action; the packet correctly remains Approved since the one-line fix already forecloses this manifestation identically to the one the PR names.
citations: xds/internal/balancer/priority/balancer.go:260-273 (run()'s select receives from the buffer before locking, so a legitimately-queued update lets run() attempt b.mu.Lock() while Close() may already hold it)
xds/internal/balancer/priority/balancer.go:218-233 (Close() holds b.mu for its whole body via defer, across b.done.Fire() and the child.stop() loop)

internal/buffer/unbounded.go:53-66,95-105 (Put/Load/Close: Close() only sets closing=true and closes the channel once the backlog is drained, so items queued before Close() begins are still delivered to run() via Get(), with ok=true, after Close() has started)
xds/internal/balancer/priority/balancer_child.go:127-138 (stop() -> stopInitTimer() sets timerW.stopped=true and calls timerW.timer.Stop() while Close() still holds b.mu)

xds/internal/balancer/priority/balancer_child.go:143-163 (the AfterFunc callback checks timerW.stopped only *after* acquiring cb.parent.mu; Timer.Stop() does not cancel or wait for an already-started callback per the time.AfterFunc/Timer.Stop() contract)

command: go run scratch/main.go (5 runs) — empirically confirms that an already-dispatched, mutex-blocked AfterFunc callback is not rescued by Stop() and is permanently stranded if another goroutine wins the next Lock() and never unlocks
items.basis: Code reading confirms all three of the reviewer's required steps: (1) run()'s select case receives from `b.childBalancerStateUpdate` and only then calls `b.mu.Lock()` (balancer.go:263-271), and `buffer.Unbounded.Close()` (internal/buffer/unbounded.go:95-105) does not immediately close the channel while a backlog remains, so an update queued just before or during `priorityBalancer.Close()` can still be delivered to run(), letting run() legitimately contend for `b.mu` while Close() holds it; (2) `stopInitTimer()` (balancer_child.go:127-138) sets `timerW.stopped` and calls `Stop()` while still holding `b.mu`, but per the documented `time.AfterFunc`/`Timer.Stop()` contract a `Stop()` call that returns false does not cancel or wait for a callback that has already started (i.e. is already blocked on `cb.parent.mu.Lock()`), and the callback's own `stopped` check only runs after it acquires the lock; (3) if the pre-fix `run()` goroutine wins the next `Lock()` after `Close()`'s `defer b.mu.Unlock()` fires and returns without unlocking, the already-blocked callback goroutine is queued on a mutex that is never released again and never gets to run its check. A standard-library scratch reproduction using the real `sync.Mutex`/`time.AfterFunc` primitives (not the clone) confirmed this is a reachable, repeatable interleaving (5/5 runs): the callback blocks before the simulated Close() releases the lock, `Stop()` returns false, a second Lock() call (modelling pre-fix run()) wins the lock and never releases it, and the callback goroutine never completes. This is a genuine, previously-unconfirmed scope expansion of the same pre-fix defect the PR fixes, reachable through purely internal balancer scheduling with no illegal external call required (unlike the PR's own named consequence, whose reachability the maintainer disputes). It does not change the verdict at the pinned head: the one-line fix makes `b.mu` unconditionally released on every return path out of `run()`, which eliminates this manifestation exactly as it eliminates the one the PR names, so it is a true but sub-threshold observation about the already-fixed pre-existing bug's scope, not a currently live defect.

N2.description: True observation that the pre-fix mutex leak in priorityBalancer.run() could also permanently strand an already-dispatched balancer_child.go init-timer AfterFunc callback (cb.parent.mu.Lock() at balancer_child.go:152), not just an UpdateClientConnState caller, via a legitimate-scheduling race for b.mu after Close() releases it: Close()'s stopInitTimer() sets timerW.stopped and calls Stop() while still holding the lock, but Stop() does not rescue a callback that has already started and is blocked waiting for that same lock, so if the pre-fix run() wins the race for the freed lock and leaks it, the callback is stuck forever. Reachable without any illegal external call, unlike the PR's own named consequence. Sub-threshold at the pinned head because the same one-line fix (unconditional b.mu.Unlock() on every return path of run()) forecloses this manifestation identically to the one the PR names — a broader, but already-remedied, scope of the same pre-existing bug.
N2.source: adjudicator, superseding this item's prior F1 concept after independent confirmation

basis: The reviewer's three required steps all check out against the code: run() can legitimately be queued on b.mu.Lock() while Close() holds it (balancer.go:260-273; internal/buffer/unbounded.go:95-105 shows Close() does not immediately close the update channel while a backlog remains); stopInitTimer()'s Stop() call (balancer_child.go:127-138) does not cancel or unblock an already-dispatched callback already waiting on cb.parent.mu (balancer_child.go:143-163), matching the documented time.AfterFunc/Timer.Stop() contract; and if pre-fix run() wins the subsequent lock race and leaks it, the blocked callback is stranded forever. A standard-library scratch program reproducing the same mutex/timer primitives confirmed this interleaving is real and repeatable (5/5 runs). The prior ruling of 'false' was wrong because it assumed the timer callback would always either finish before Close() begins or be the one granted the lock immediately after Close()'s defer fires; Go's sync.Mutex explicitly does not guarantee waiter ordering in its normal (non-starvation) mode, so run() can win that race instead, which the code does not forbid.

commands_run.summary: Located exact line numbers for run()'s select/Lock/Unlock structure to confirm run() locks after receiving from the buffer.

Confirmed Close() only sets closing=true and closes the channel once the backlog is empty, so pre-queued items are still delivered to run() via Get() with ok=true after priorityBalancer.Close() begins.

Standard-library reproduction (run 5 times) using real sync.Mutex/time.AfterFunc/Timer.Stop(): an already-blocked AfterFunc callback is not rescued by Stop() and is permanently stranded when a second goroutine wins the next Lock() and never unlocks; reproduced deterministically in all 5 runs.
Confirmed the clone remained unmodified; scratch program lives only under the adjudication working directory and depends only on the Go standard library.

notes: The original ruling missed that Go's sync.Mutex provides no ordering guarantee among multiple already-blocked waiters in its default (non-starvation) mode, and that time.Timer.Stop() does not rescue an AfterFunc callback that has already started and is blocked acquiring a mutex elsewhere -- it only prevents a *future* firing. Once both facts are accounted for, the interleaving the reviewer describes is real and reachable, confirmed both by code reading (balancer.go, balancer_child.go, internal/buffer/unbounded.go) and by an independent standard-library scratch reproduction using the same primitives. The item's ruling changes from false/not-applicable to supported/sub-threshold (concept renamed from F1 to N2); this does not change the packet's overall Approved status, its explicit clean claim, or any action/priority assessment, since the item was already filed as a non-blocking observation and remains non-material at the pinned head (the one-line fix already forecloses this manifestation along with the one the PR names). A future v2 register could reasonably add this as a seventh 'Not ground truth' entry alongside the existing six, rather than as a new defect ID, since it is scope on the same already-fixed bug, not a separate unfixed defect.
